$comment: Allowlist for check_fact_category_pinning.py (brief §5 C.7, SUDDHA-VACA Phase C lane:ci-lint). Every entry requires: file (repo-relative POSIX path, must match a Violation.file exactly), EITHER line (int, matched exactly against the violation's line number) OR pattern (a string matched as a regex, falling back to a plain substring match, against the violation's snippet text) — line is preferred when known since it is unambiguous; pattern is for cases where line drift is expected, and justification (a non-empty, specific, human-readable reason — 'pre-existing' alone is not sufficient, say WHY it's safe or why it's out of scope). An entry with neither line nor pattern never matches anything (fails closed, not open). Populated 2026-07-28 during the initial rollout scan against the live repo tree (this worktree, base main, before this wave's other lanes landed) — see the ci-lint lane's session report for the full disposition rationale of every entry.

entries.justification: AUDITED source-query availability probe for get_strength, not a value read or one-row reduction. The SELECT deliberately reproduces the handler's complete 21-category default source scope (STRENGTH_CATEGORIES) while LIMIT 0 guarantees that no fact row is selected — availability is earned solely by authenticated query success against the chart's served build set, including a legitimate empty category set. Adding an arbitrary fact_key predicate would narrow the real handler contract (get_strength.ts serves all 21 categories by default and any subset on request) and could report availability while a valid strength category remains unreadable. The chart+served-build binding and intentional zero-row shape are exercised by availability_coverage.test.ts.

entries.pattern: SELECT fact_id, fact_subject FROM chart_facts WHERE chart_id = %s AND ayanamsha_id = %s AND fact_category = 'sensitive_degree_check'
entries.justification: AUDITED set-valued whole-category read (2026-09-29, l3/gochara-autonomous-wp0-7), bo_upaya.py precedent. The result builds a fact_id -> fact_subject map over EVERY 'sensitive_degree_check' row (facts.sensitive_checks, line 269-271) used later only as a membership/lookup table (line 346). No row is selected or reduced by fact_category alone; there is no single-row misselection surface. Pinning one fact_key would BREAK the semantics (the map needs all keys of the category).

entries.pattern: SELECT fact_subject, fact_key, fact_value_text, fact_value_num FROM chart_facts WHERE chart_id = %s AND fact_category = 'ashtakavarga_kakshya_boundary'
entries.justification: AUDITED set-valued multi-key assembler (2026-09-29, l3/gochara-autonomous-wp0-7), get_kp_cusps.ts:140 precedent. _fetch_kakshya_boundaries reads EVERY fact_key of the category and assembles a per-subject dict keyed BY fact_key (start_deg/end_deg/lord per kakshya); the engine consumes the assembled boundary set, never a category-only row. A single fact_key pin would drop the sibling keys the assembler requires. Empty-set fallback is honest (WP5 H-1a flag).
